analyst_view.overall: Cádiz (17th, 14 points) host Córdoba (8th, 23 points, one point off the play-off places) at Nuevo Mirandilla on Sunday in an Andalusian derby. Cádiz, under Borja Jiménez, have climbed three places in three weeks and just won 3-0 at Real Sociedad B, though they have taken few points at home this season; Córdoba are unbeaten in six league games and won 3-0 at Oviedo last time, scoring 28 goals in 15 games but also conceding 25. Córdoba captain Cristian Carracedo is banned for five yellow cards (confirmed by EFE, counted by the numbers), and Cádiz are without Tabatadze (long-term, counted). The derby is not flagged in the numbers, which is the one thing I add; no referee is named and news on both squads was thin.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals, already taking about 7% off Córdoba for Carracedo's ban. Córdoba have scored 14 in their last six and conceded plenty all season, and Cádiz just scored three away, all counted by the momentum figures; with no new absences found in either attack, I stay at 2.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.7 corners, already adding about 10% to Córdoba for their 51 corners in six games. Carracedo plays wide on the right, but Córdoba's wide play has carried their corner counts all season and the numbers count his ban, so I stay at 10.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.8 cards, already raising Córdoba for 23 cards in their last six. I lean slightly higher, +4% to about 6.0, because this is an Andalusian derby the numbers do not flag, with Cádiz near the drop zone and Córdoba chasing the play-offs; it stays mild because the rivalry is not among the fiercest and no referee is named.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.1 shots, with Córdoba expected to take more (16.1). Córdoba's open, attacking style (they average about 1.9 goals scored and 1.7 conceded) and Cádiz's recent shot counts are already in the numbers, and no lineup news changes either side's volume, so I stay at 28.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target, already nudging Córdoba up for 38 on target in their last six. Their top scorer Percan and Cádiz's Cordero are not reported missing, and Carracedo's ban is counted, so I stay at 9.3.
